raw_segments.text: To be sure, it was a deserted place, down to the pigeon house in the brewery yard, which
had been blown crooked on its pole by some high wind, and would have made the pigeons
think themselves at sea if there had been any pigeons there to be rocked by it.
But there were no pigeons in the dove cot, no horses in the stable, no pigs in the stye,
no malt in the storehouse, no smells of grains and beer in the copper or the vat.
All the uses and scents of the brewery might have evaporated with its last reek of smoke.
In a by-yard, there was a wilderness of empty casks, which had a certain sour remembrance
of better days lingering about them.
But it was too sour to be accepted as a sample of the beer that was gone.
And in this respect, I remember those recluses as being like most others.
